observed_mechanics: 0x00642210 PUSH ESI -- saves ESI; this is the single frame instruction, and it is what makes ESP at 0x00642218 equal entry_ESP-4.

0x00642211 MOV ESI,ECX -- the only read of ECX in the body (obs-0002), and the machine record names that register as the RECEIVER (receiver.register ECX, provenance vftable_slot_dispatch, INFERRED). ECX is not written again anywhere in these 30 bytes, so it still holds the entry value at the 0x00642213 call. The copy into ESI buys lifetime across both calls: the body never dereferences ESI or ECX in any register.
0x00642213 CALL 0x00642190 -- direct, rel32, NO argument pushed and no stack adjustment on either side. Unconditional: nothing precedes it but the two instructions above and no branch skips it.

0x00642218 TEST byte ptr [ESP + 0x8],0x1 -- the body's ONLY memory operand and its only immediate. ESP+0x8 resolves to entry_ESP+0x4 because exactly one word (PUSH ESI) is outstanding and the 0x00642213 call has returned: the slot is the caller's first stack argument, not a frame slot and not a field.

0x00642218 reads ONE BYTE (the operand is `byte ptr`, obs-0006 size 1) and tests bit 0 against the immediate 1. The other seven bits of that byte are not examined and the other three bytes of the slot are neither read nor written.
0x0064221d JZ 0x00642228 -- the single conditional branch, and its target 0x00642228 is INSIDE the body span (0x00642210..0x0064222b), so the branch graph is closed.
0x0064221f PUSH ESI -- the boundary word goes on the stack for the cdecl callee. Same word as the ECX one: nothing between 0x00642211 and here writes ECX or ESI.
0x00642220 CALL 0x00f47380 -- direct, rel32, one stack word outstanding.

0x00642225 ADD ESP,0x4 -- the BODY drops the word it pushed, so the cleanup is on the caller's side of this call. That is the cdecl shape and it is the one calling convention this listing does settle, for this internal call.

0x00642228 MOV EAX,ESI -- the return value is the entry word. It is reached by the JZ on the bit-clear path and by falling out of the ADD on the bit-set path, so BOTH paths return the same value. It also overwrites whatever 0x00f47380 left in EAX, three instructions after that call, so the second callee's result is unreachable to the caller.
0x0064222b RET 0x4 -- pops the return address and drops 4 bytes of arguments: stack_cleanup_bytes 4, owner callee, confidence OBSERVED.
Both paths converge on the single RET. There is exactly one return site in the body.
The body writes nothing through any pointer: it contains no store instruction and its only memory operand is a byte TEST against a stack slot.
The body performs no virtual dispatch: both callees are immediate operands, matching the machine dispatch record's indirect_calls 0 and vtable_shaped_loads 0.

CONVENTION. The machine record determines __thiscall (INFERRED, single candidate): R1-VFT from the vftable slot at 0x013ff648 plus the body reading its incoming ECX, C6B from the callee-side cleanup. Two independent machine facts corroborate it from the caller side: there is no direct CALL into this address anywhere, and the only two code entries are the SUB ECX,0x10 / JMP stub at 0x00642170/0x00642173 and the SUB ECX,0x14 / JMP stub at 0x00642180/0x00642183.

ENTRY SHAPE. The two entry stubs prove the receiver is reached at two different displacements and that this body adjusts nothing itself, which is why the receiver's identity relative to any base address is UNRESOLVED rather than merely unnamed.
semantic_findings: The body is a two-callee wrapper with one bit gate. 0x00642190 always runs; 0x00f47380 runs only when bit 0 of the caller's first stack byte is set; the entry word is returned either way.

The gate is a MASK, not a truth test. TEST byte ptr [ESP + 0x8],0x1 means 0x02, 0x04, 0x40 and 0x80 are FALSE. Any reconstruction spelling the argument as bool, or writing `if (flag)`, is wrong on every even nonzero value. This is the single most discriminating fact in the body and it is why StackArgument is uint8_t and the model test drives all 256 values.

The two callees provably receive the SAME word: ECX is written once (by the caller) and ESI once (0x00642211), and neither is touched again before both calls. A reconstruction passing the flag, or the return value, or different words to the two callees is refuted.

The return is the entry word on both paths and is never either callee's result. 0x00642228 is unconditional and follows 0x00642220 by three instructions, so the second callee's return value is discarded.

The receiver is present in ECX and is never dereferenced. Those are two separate facts and the second is the sharp one: the body copies the receiver, hands it to both callees and returns it, and not one of those operations inspects it. The machine record agrees (receiver present true, register ECX, bounds_only true, offsets []). The type is therefore an undefined struct -- no pointee, no field, no size -- even though the register carries a receiver. An earlier revision of this package read the absence of a dereference as the absence of a receiver, which the machine record now corrects: R1-VFT places the receiver from the vftable slot, not from a dereference.

No virtual dispatch is performed by the body, and no class is claimed. The record does associate this VA with vtable:0x013ff648, and that association is the EVIDENCE for the receiver (receiver_provenance vftable_slot_dispatch), not a claim that the body dispatches: the body contains no indirect transfer at all, and it is a slot occupant rather than a dispatcher. A slot is not a class, and this binary carries no MSVC RTTI.

Cleanup is asymmetric between the two calls and that asymmetry is the evidence: 0x00642190 takes nothing on the stack and nothing is adjusted for it, while 0x00f47380 takes one word that the body itself drops. The OUTER RET 0x4 then pops the CALLER's one word. Three different stack effects in thirty bytes, and the outer one is what C6B combines with the ECX receiver to name __thiscall.

The two stack effects on the way IN are the discriminator the whole body turns on: the receiver arrives in ECX and the option word arrives at entry_ESP+0x4, and they are different values. The only entries into the body are two JMPs from caller-side ECX adjustors, which is the shape of a receiver being passed and not of a by-value first argument being passed.
unresolved_questions: THE RECEIVER'S IDENTITY. __thiscall says the receiver arrives in ECX; it does not say what the receiver IS. This body never dereferences it and never adjusts it, and the two entry stubs adjust ECX by 0x10 and 0x14 before arriving, so at least two different base relationships reach 0x00642210. No class, no vtable identity, no receiver type, no object size, no vtable-pointer offset and no field are claimed, and the base relationships are not guessed.

WHETHER THE RECEIVER IS A POINTER AT ALL. It is a 32-bit word that is copied, passed in a register, pushed and returned. Nothing in these 30 bytes inspects it, so nothing here can say whether it addresses an object. The type is left undefined (struct Receiver;) and no pointee is named.

WHAT 0x00f47380 IS. Unnamed in the image (FUN_00f47380), owned by no package, and given a semantic name by nothing here. It is an observer in this package's model test. The one machine fact this package holds about it is the call shape: one cdecl dword, dropped by the body at 0x00642225.

WHAT 0x00642190 DOES. Owned by pkg-swarm-w1 as sporepedia_asset_destroy_00642190. This package reads none of that package's source and asserts only that its call here is unconditional, passes nothing on the stack, and hands over the receiver in ECX. The two packages' claims are independent.

THE RETURNED VALUE'S C TYPE. The machine fixes the WIDTH (4 bytes; MOV EAX,ESI at 0x00642228 is the last write before the sole return on both paths) and the FACT that the value is the receiver. It does not fix the type: Receiver *, uint32_t or any other four-byte spelling are all consistent with it. Receiver * is the declared source-side choice, not a recovered fact.

WHETHER THE OPTION WORD'S UPPER 24 BITS CARRY MEANING. The machine reads one byte and tests one bit. The other three bytes of the four-byte slot are untouched here, but a caller may have put something in them, and nothing in this body constrains them.

THE CLASS THAT OWNS THE TABLE 0x013ff648, AND WHETHER IT IS A vptr-BACKED VTABLE AT ALL. R1-VFT calls the table it reasons about a sound vptr-backed vftable, and GhidraMCP /read_memory at 0x013ff640 for 24 bytes shows a table whose first slot is this body, but this binary carries no MSVC RTTI and no SDK name is recorded for the table. The receiver determination does not need a class and none is claimed.

WHETHER THE ENTRY STUBS 0x00642170 AND 0x00642180 BELONG TO THIS BODY'S OWN CLASS OR TO A DERIVED ONE. Two caller-side this-adjustors is the shape of multiple inheritance adjustment, but the object model behind them is not in evidence here and is not assumed.

mutation_evidence.note: The four SM mutations are the ones that matter for the byte witness: the emitted code and the header transcript are changed TOGETHER, so case W cannot see them and only executed behaviour can kill them. They do. Conversely M1 and M15, which change the bytes without the transcript, are killed by the byte comparison alone -- which is the point of pinning the reconstruction to the binary's own /read_memory output rather than to a second assembly of the same instructions.

notes: No validation check was weakened, disabled or special-cased. tools/reconstruction_tooling/validate.py, abi_infer.py and every other file under tools/ were not modified, no test under tests/ was modified, no validation report was edited, and reconstruction/knowledge/index.json was not hand-edited: the validator rebuilds its index ephemerically from the canonical inputs, of which this sidecar is one. Nothing was committed to git and nothing under src/ was touched.

The convention this package now declares is the machine's, transcribed field for field from evidence pack category abi_derived, and it is carried in the staging header as data rather than only in prose so that a later edit that reverts it fails the model test instead of passing quietly. The previous revision of this package deliberately declared no convention and this sidecar deliberately recorded none, for as long as the derived record abstained; every sentence that asserted that abstention has been rewritten or deleted here rather than left standing next to the new determination.

The caller-side corroboration is recorded as CORROBORATION and not as the source of the claim. The two this-adjusting JMP stubs are real machine facts (GhidraMCP /disassemble_bytes at 0x00642150..0x0064218f), they do exclude the pack's former other candidate __stdcall, and they are not what R1-VFT or C6B used. One correction to the earlier worker briefing: it named the two adjustors as 0x00642160 and 0x00642170, whereas the SUB ECX instructions are at 0x00642170 and 0x00642180; the JMP addresses it gave, 0x00642173 and 0x00642183, are correct. The sidecar carries the addresses as read from the image.

One harness bug was found and fixed in this package's own model test during the run. The first revision of the call harness planted an ESI sentinel and never gave ESI back, so it corrupted its own caller -- an i386 SysV cdecl function must preserve ESI. It was fixed by saving the caller's ESI into the probe's own frame (B-40) and restoring it before `leave`. A second bug in the same file was found by inspection rather than by a compiler: a case handed the entry an UNMAPPED receiver (0x5eed1234) to show it is never dereferenced, and segfaulted -- not in the body, which never dereferences it, but in the model test's own teardown observer, which does. It was replaced by a case using a distinct mapped object, and the comment there now says plainly that a receiver has to be mapped because the OBSERVERS dereference it, not because the body needs to.
